liebermann.description_de: London Lambeth 118 (einst ecclesia de Merton, dann [Lord] Lumby gehörig)
liebermann.shelfmark_as_given: London, Lambeth Palace Library, MS 118 (formerly of Merton priory, then Lord Lumley’s)
liebermann.laws: In Cn, Wl art, ECf retr
liebermann.notes: Henry of Huntingdon, c. 1190, once of Merton and then Lord Lumley: In Cn after the history of Cnut (ff. 94–104); after the chronicle (f. 194) the Tripartita with rubricator II (Wl art, rubric list to ECf, ECf retr) and Genealogia Normannica to 1154; f. 206 a computation of the capture of Jerusalem 1099; on the last page (14th c.) Wl art again to c. 7. The best manuscript of Ip Hunt, resembling Additional 21088 and La, ending with a colophon verse; copied in Harley 596.

others.text: O’Brien (2003): O’Brien calls this manuscript La (not to be confused with Liebermann’s La, Lambeth 179): the earliest copy of the fifth edition, version B, of Henry of Huntingdon. In the stretch O’Brien checked (title, prologue, I 1–3) he found 54 errors in Liebermann’s readings, 33 of them from Lb and S: e.g. Lb reads Anglie not Anglice, Norag- not Norwag-, Kannuto not Canuto, mundbreche not mundbrece, omits scilicet at I 2,2.
